library(tidyverse)
# Add any other libraries here
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
Raw Variable Name Clean Variable Name Data Type Numerical or Categorical Description & Units
Date date chr categorical date in year-month-day format
Rented Bike Count rented_bike_count dbl numerical count of bikes rented at each hour
Hour hour dbl numerical hour of the day
Temperature temperature_c dbl numerical temperature in Celsius
Humidity humidity_percent dbl numerical humidity in percentage
Wind Speed wind_speed_m_s dbl numerical wind speed in m/s
Visibility visibility_10m dbl numerical visibility in 10m units
Dew Point Temperature dew_point_temperature_c dbl numerical dew point temperature - temperature at which the air needs to be cooled to (at constant pressure) in order to achieve a relative humidity
Solar Radiation solar_radiation_mj_m2 dbl numerical solar radiation in MJ/M^2
Rainfall rainfall_mm dbl numerical rainfall in mm
Snowfall snowfall_cm dbl numerical snowfall in cm
Seasons seasons chr categorical represents the four seasons
Holiday holiday chr categorical holiday or no holiday
Functioning Day functioning_day chr categorical yes or no; represents if system is fully operational or not

Questions

  1. Does temperature affect bike demand differently during peak commuting hours (8-9am and 6-7pm) compared to off-peak hours?
  2. Is the holiday effect uniform across seasons, or do holiday demand patterns shift significantly between the seasons?
  3. Is there a sharp threshold or non-linear drop-off point where precipitation severly degrades demand, or is the decay linear?
  4. How do temperature and humidity combine to affect demand (compared to just considering temperature)?
  5. How does the hourly distribution shift between a regular working day and a non-working day?
# load your data 
seoul_bikes_raw <- read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale=locale(encoding="latin1")) #extracting raw data, locale needed to be specified as error otherwise.
## Rows: 8760 Columns: 14
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr  (4): Date, Seasons, Holiday, Functioning Day
## dbl (10): Rented Bike Count, Hour, Temperature(°C), Humidity(%), Wind speed ...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
seoul_bikes <- seoul_bikes_raw |> clean_names() #cleaning names to snake_case, as column headings' words initially separated with space
seoul_bikes
## # A tibble: 8,760 × 14
##    date    rented_bike_count  hour temperature_c humidity_percent wind_speed_m_s
##    <chr>               <dbl> <dbl>         <dbl>            <dbl>          <dbl>
##  1 01/12/…               254     0          -5.2               37            2.2
##  2 01/12/…               204     1          -5.5               38            0.8
##  3 01/12/…               173     2          -6                 39            1  
##  4 01/12/…               107     3          -6.2               40            0.9
##  5 01/12/…                78     4          -6                 36            2.3
##  6 01/12/…               100     5          -6.4               37            1.5
##  7 01/12/…               181     6          -6.6               35            1.3
##  8 01/12/…               460     7          -7.4               38            0.9
##  9 01/12/…               930     8          -7.6               37            1.1
## 10 01/12/…               490     9          -6.5               27            0.5
## # ℹ 8,750 more rows
## # ℹ 8 more variables: visibility_10m <dbl>, dew_point_temperature_c <dbl>,
## #   solar_radiation_mj_m2 <dbl>, rainfall_mm <dbl>, snowfall_cm <dbl>,
## #   seasons <chr>, holiday <chr>, functioning_day <chr>
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

seoul_bikes <- seoul_bikes %>%
  mutate(
    wind_group = cut(
      wind_speed_m_s,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 1, 2, 3, 4, Inf),
      labels = c("0-1", "1-2", "2-3", "3-4", "4+")
    )
  )

ggplot(seoul_bikes,
       aes(x = wind_group,
           y = rented_bike_count)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "col",
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Bike Rentals at Different Wind Speeds",
    x = "Wind Speed (m/s)",
    y = "Average Number of Bikes Rented"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Initial Plots

seoul_bikes |>  ggplot(data = _, mapping = aes(x = temperature_c, y = rented_bike_count)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = holiday, alpha = visibility_10m, shape = seasons)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) + 
  facet_wrap( ~ holiday) +
  labs(x = "Temperature",
       y = "Rent Bike Count",
       title = "How Temperatures Affects the Quantity of Bikes Rented",
       colour = "Holiday",
       shape = "Season",
       alpha = "Visibility (10m)"
      )
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'gam' and formula = 'y ~ s(x, bs = "cs")'

#will need scaling later to make sure points are more visible

seoul_bikes |>  ggplot(data = _, mapping = aes(x = temperature_c, y = rented_bike_count)) +
  geom_bin_2d()
## `stat_bin2d()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

seoul_bikes |> ggplot(data = _, mapping = aes(x = rented_bike_count, fill = seasons)) +
  geom_density(mapping = aes(alpha = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~ holiday, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)

seoul_bikes |> ggplot(data = _, mapping = aes(x = rented_bike_count, fill = seasons)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  facet_grid(seasons ~ holiday, scales = "free")

seoul_bikes |> ggplot(data = _, mapping = aes(x = seasons, y = rented_bike_count)) +
  geom_boxplot()

seoul_bikes |> ggplot(mapping = aes(x = rented_bike_count, fill = holiday, alpha = 0.1)) +
  geom_density()

seoul_bikes |> ggplot(mapping = aes(x = hour, y = rented_bike_count)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(seasons ~ holiday, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)

seoul_bikes |> mutate(
  snow = ifelse(snowfall_cm == 0, FALSE, TRUE)
) |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = rented_bike_count, color = snow, alpha = 0.1)) +
  geom_density() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)
